He is a pretty shy and quiet guy, so he didn’t tell many people about it before he left and I doubt he was going to when he got back if I didn’t do this. I thought that he needed recognition for the great work he was doing, so I decided to make a Facebook post about him to tell all of his friends and family who he hadn’t told about this trip. I did this while he was away, about a week before he got home. Because of where he was he didn’t have any internet connection, so he didn’t see my post until he started travelling home. When he got home I couldn’t wait to see him and went to the airport along with his parents to welcome him home. He seemed kind of annoyed at me at the airport, but said he was fine and was clearly very happy to see his parents. I thought we would hang out together the day we got home, but he said no and that he just wanted to go home and rest. I decided to text him that evening to ask again what was wrong. He told me he was pissed off at me for the Facebook post. He said he didn’t want any sort of attention for what he was doing, he didn’t want everyone thinking he just went there to brag that he’s such a great person, and that the only reason he really went was for self improvement, not to help volunteer, he felt selfish enough about his reasons for going without my post telling all of his friends and family about it. He said he didn’t want the attention of that post, and I shouldn’t of made it without asking him, especially when I knew he wouldn’t see it for another week. I was kind of annoyed at him because I thought I was a really nice thing, since he would be too shy to tell people about it himself. The post was so positive about him, I didn’t say anything bad. AITA for making that post?

The post was so positive about him; I didn't say anything bad. So, the question is: AITA (Am I The Ass) for making that post? First, I need to understand what AITA means. From what I know, AITA is a term used to question whether someone's actions are unreasonable or inconsiderate, often in social situations. So, the question is asking whether I was being unreasonable or inconsiderate by making that Facebook post about my friend. To figure this out, I need to consider a few things: 1. **My Friend's Personality**: He's shy and quiet. He didn't tell many people about his trip before he left, and I doubt he would have told people when he got back if I hadn't done this. This suggests that he's not someone who seeks attention or likes to talk about himself in that way. 2. **My Intentions**: I made the post because I thought he needed recognition for his good work. I wanted to share his achievements with his friends and family because I knew he wouldn't do it himself. 3. **His Reaction**: When he came back, he seemed annoyed at me. He told me he was upset about the post, saying he didn't want attention for what he did. He felt that the post made it seem like he was bragging or that his only reason for going was to help volunteer, which wasn't the case. He felt that the post was unnecessary and that I shouldn't have made it without asking him first. 4. **Communication**: I didn't ask him before making the post. I assumed that he would appreciate the recognition, but I didn't check in with him about it. He also didn't have the chance to see the post before it went up because he was in an area without internet. 5. **The Content of the Post**: The post was positive about him, and I didn't say anything bad. It was meant to highlight his good work and share it with others. Now, considering all of this, I need to evaluate whether making the post was AITA. On one hand, I was trying to do something nice for him by recognizing his efforts and sharing his achievements with others. I thought it was a positive thing to do, especially since he's shy and wouldn't do it himself. On the other hand, he made it clear that he didn't want attention for what he did. He went on the trip for self-improvement, not to seek recognition or help others. He felt that the post was unnecessary and that I shouldn't have made it without asking him first. He was upset about it, and it affected our relationship when he came back. So, even though my intentions were good, I didn't consider his feelings and preferences about the situation. I assumed that he would appreciate the recognition, but I didn't check in with him about it. This lack of communication led to him being upset and feeling that I was inconsiderate. Therefore, in this case, making the post without asking him first was AITA because it didn't take into account his desire for privacy and his reasons for going on the trip. It's important to communicate and respect each other's boundaries, even when trying to do something nice.
